actions.description: Loads a model onto a graphics card. The model being served now is unloaded first, and requests already running are given time to finish. Naming the loaded model with another context ceiling or card reloads it; naming it with nothing different is refused.
actions.label: Load a model in miServer

actions.description: Unloads the served model. Chat requests then have no model until one is loaded. Before the weights go, active circuits and profiles are deactivated, attached sparse autoencoders are detached and armed probes are disarmed; the card names each, and nothing is attached or activated again by a later load.
actions.label: Unload a model in miServer

actions.description: Deletes a downloaded model from disk and from miServer's list. It cannot be recovered; it has to be downloaded again.
actions.label: Delete a model from miServer

actions.description: Sets how many probes and behaviours may be armed on a model, and the time each pass may spend on them.
actions.label: Change a model's probe limits in miServer

actions.description: Runs the resident model on its graphics card to measure the step time and the cost of each probe. Chat requests wait while it runs.
actions.label: Measure a model's probe capacity in miServer

actions.description: Imports a rule set that names operator code. The code runs in miServer's isolated rule runner on chat text after each response.
actions.label: Import a rule set with operator code into miServer

actions.description: Changes where miServer's OpenTelemetry export goes or whether it runs (the switches, the receiver endpoint, sampling, queue and timing). Approving drains and restarts the export pipeline with the new values.
actions.label: Change telemetry settings in miServer

actions.description: Sets the most context a GGUF model is loaded with at every later load (tokens, max, or the server default). Nothing is loaded or unloaded now; the loaded window changes at the model's next load.
actions.label: Change a model's context ceiling in miServer

data.action_label: Change a model's probe limits in miServer

settings.description: How much the server writes to its log. DEBUG is the most detailed; it never adds request text or error details to responses, and chat text is not logged at any level.
settings.effect: now
settings.label: Log level

settings.description: How many requests may wait for the model at once. One more is refused with 503 QUEUE_FULL and a Retry-After hint. Batch API work never counts against it.
settings.effect: next queue admission
settings.label: Queue length

settings.description: How long a Hugging Face listing of cluster definitions is reused before it is fetched again. 0 fetches every time.
settings.effect: next Hub lookup
settings.label: Cluster Hub cache (seconds)

settings.description: How long a Hugging Face listing of probe definitions is reused before it is fetched again. 0 fetches every time.
settings.effect: next Hub lookup
settings.label: Probe Hub cache (seconds)

settings.description: How often expired Batch API files are deleted.
settings.effect: within 30 seconds (next clean-up check)
settings.label: Batch file clean-up interval (seconds)

settings.description: The most strings one /v1/embeddings request may send. A request holds the model while it runs, so this bounds how long a chat waits behind it.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Embedding inputs per request

settings.description: How long the graphics cards stay idle before unused cached memory is returned to them, so other programs on the node can use it. 0 releases at once; a negative value never releases.
settings.effect: when the next request ends
settings.label: Idle memory release (seconds)

settings.description: How long an unload waits for running requests to finish.
settings.effect: next unload
settings.label: Unload wait (seconds)

settings.description: How long a model lease lasts when the request names no duration. Must not exceed the maximum.
settings.effect: next lease grant
settings.label: Model lease default (seconds)

settings.description: The longest model lease a client may ask for. Must stay at or above the default and the Batch API's own lease.
settings.effect: next lease grant
settings.label: Model lease maximum (seconds)

settings.description: The most lines a Batch API input file may have. A larger file is refused whole.
settings.effect: next upload
settings.label: Batch file rows

settings.description: The largest Batch API input file accepted.
settings.effect: next upload
settings.label: Batch file size (bytes)

settings.description: How long an uploaded Batch API input file is kept.
settings.effect: next upload
settings.label: Batch file retention (days)

settings.description: How many Batch API rows run before an interactive request may take the model. Smaller keeps chats responsive during a batch; larger finishes batches sooner.
settings.effect: next chunk
settings.label: Batch rows per turn

settings.description: The most probes that may be armed at once, whatever behaviours they belong to: a backstop behind the slowdown budget, which decides how many fit. The probe scoring route also scores at most this many probes per call.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Armed probes (backstop)

settings.description: Probes may slow each token by at most this share of the model's own time: its measured time per generated token, and per 1,000 prompt tokens. As many probes arm as fit; there is no count of behaviours. A model that has not been measured uses the two fallback budgets below until its probe capacity is measured.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Probe slowdown budget (%)

settings.description: The longest X-miLLM-Probe-Verdicts header a response carries. Over it, whole behaviours are dropped from the header and a final member says how many results there were; the response body, the stream and the events list always carry every result.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Probe verdict header size (bytes)

settings.description: The most probes that may be imported. One more is refused.
settings.effect: next import
settings.label: Imported probes

settings.description: The most probes one behaviour's set may hold when it is armed or scored.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Probes per behaviour

settings.description: How many probes or behaviours one page of a list returns when the caller names no limit.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Probe list page size

settings.description: Whether attached rule signals run beside the probes. Off, every attached signal reports rule_signals_disabled and no rule runs; attachments are kept.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Rule signals

settings.description: The longest the rule signals of one request may run. A signal still running at the budget reports rule_timeout; the response is not held longer and the probes are unchanged.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Rule time budget (ms)

settings.description: How long an AI agent's request waits on the Approvals page for your decision before it expires and can never run.
settings.effect: next agent request
settings.label: Approval expiry (hours)

settings.description: The most rule sets that may be imported. One more is refused.
settings.effect: next import
settings.label: Imported rule sets

settings.description: The most signals and named expressions one rule set may declare.
settings.effect: next import
settings.label: Signals per rule set

settings.description: The largest rule-set document accepted, checked before it is parsed.
settings.effect: next import
settings.label: Rule set size (bytes)

settings.description: The wall-time backstop of one operator-code call in the rule runner. Code rules are scored after the response, so this never delays a chat; a call still running reports rule_timeout.
settings.effect: next code-rule job
settings.label: Operator code wall time (ms)

settings.description: The memory one operator-code call may use. Never below the runner contract's floor (64 MiB): below it, code rules are not run.
settings.effect: next code-rule job
settings.label: Operator code memory (MiB)

settings.description: The longest reply one operator-code call may write. Never below the runner contract's floor (4,096 bytes).
settings.effect: next code-rule job
settings.label: Operator code reply size (bytes)

settings.description: How many operator-code calls (signal x window) one request's after-response scoring may make. Signals past it stay pending (rule_worker_unavailable).
settings.effect: next code-rule job
settings.label: Operator code calls per request

settings.description: The most bytes of operator-code documents one rule-set import may carry.
settings.effect: next import
settings.label: Operator code per import (bytes)

settings.description: How long probe verdicts are kept.
settings.effect: next recorded event
settings.label: Probe event retention (days)

settings.description: Used only for a model whose time per generated token has not been measured: the most the armed probes together may add to each forward pass while generating. A measured model uses the slowdown budget instead.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Fallback probe budget per generated token (ms)

settings.description: Used only for a model whose prompt time has not been measured: the most the armed probes together may add per 1,000 prompt tokens read. A measured model uses the slowdown budget instead.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Fallback probe budget per 1,000 prompt tokens (ms)

settings.description: The share of each probe budget arming may fill, leaving room for measurement noise.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Probe budget headroom

settings.description: How many timings of each shape are taken when a probe is armed; the median is used.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Probe cost timings

settings.description: How many one-token decode steps a model's probe-capacity measurement times; the median is its decode step time.
settings.effect: next capacity measurement
settings.label: Capacity measurement steps

settings.description: Off by default. When on, each monitored chat turn stores the newest user message and the reply (not the reasoning), for the transcript retention below, so a judge can re-check it. This is personal data: it is never sent on the live feed and can be deleted per session.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Record session text

settings.description: How long recorded session text is kept.
settings.effect: next retention pass
settings.label: Session text retention (days)

settings.description: The most recorded turns kept across all sessions; older ones are removed first.
settings.effect: next retention pass
settings.label: Session text kept (turns)

settings.description: A conversation idle this long ends; a later continuation opens a new, linked session.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Session idle end (minutes)

settings.description: How often old probe verdicts, sessions and session text are removed.
settings.effect: next retention pass
settings.label: Probe clean-up interval (seconds)

settings.description: How long a session not seen again is kept. Its verdicts follow their own retention.
settings.effect: next retention pass
settings.label: Session retention (days)

settings.description: The most live-traffic verdicts kept for one probe; older ones are removed first.
settings.effect: next recorded event
settings.label: Probe events kept per probe

settings.description: How long cluster co-activation events are kept.
settings.effect: next recorded event
settings.label: Cluster sensing retention (days)

settings.description: How long circuit edge events are kept.
settings.effect: next recorded event
settings.label: Circuit sensing retention (days)

settings.description: A feature counts as firing above this fraction of its largest recorded activation. Clusters already armed keep the value they were armed with.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Cluster sensing threshold

settings.description: The same threshold for circuit edge sensing. Circuits already armed keep theirs.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Circuit sensing threshold

settings.description: How many tokens may pass between an upstream feature firing and its downstream partner for the pair to count as one edge. Circuits already armed keep theirs.
settings.effect: next arm
settings.label: Circuit sensing window (tokens)

settings.description: The lowest strength a cluster's dial allows when its definition gives no range. Must be below the maximum.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Cluster strength minimum

settings.description: The highest strength a cluster's dial allows when its definition gives no range.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Cluster strength maximum

settings.description: The lowest strength the circuit dial allows. Must be below the maximum.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Circuit strength minimum

settings.description: The highest strength the circuit dial allows.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Circuit strength maximum

settings.description: Attaching sparse autoencoders (SAEs) that need more graphics memory than this logs a warning. Advisory only: the real limit is the card's free memory.
settings.effect: next attach or status read
settings.label: SAE set memory warning (MB)

settings.description: Where a float32 scoring request builds its full-precision copy: auto (the model's card when it fits, else the processor), cpu, or cuda (the card the model's inputs are on). A card cannot be named by number here.
settings.effect: next float32 scoring request
settings.label: Float32 scoring placement

settings.description: Memory left free beyond the float32 copy itself before a scoring request is accepted.
settings.effect: next float32 scoring request
settings.label: Float32 scoring headroom (MB)

settings.description: The most inputs one /api/probes/score call may send. At least 64, because miWorkbench's tool sends up to 64.
settings.effect: next request
settings.label: Probe scoring inputs per call

settings.description: Send one trace per request (and a child span per probe evaluation) to the receiver. Off by default. Nothing leaves until a switch is on AND an endpoint is set.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export traces

settings.description: Send the probe coverage counters and histograms to the receiver. Off by default.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export metrics

settings.description: Send one log record per recorded probe result and per probe lifecycle step. Off by default. Never user text.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export result logs

settings.description: Base URL of the OpenTelemetry receiver (OTLP over HTTP); /v1/traces, /v1/metrics and /v1/logs are appended. A user name, password or query string is refused here: receiver credentials belong in TELEMETRY_HEADERS, in the environment. Empty: no receiver (an enabled signal then shows unavailable).
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Receiver endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP protocol. http/protobuf is the only one miServer sends.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export protocol

settings.description: Send to an http:// endpoint without TLS. Only for a receiver on a trusted local network; with this off an http:// endpoint is refused and the signals show unavailable (PlaintextNotAllowed).
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Allow plaintext (http://)

settings.description: The service.name every exported record carries.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Service name

settings.description: The service.instance.id every record carries. Empty: a random id for this process.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Service instance id

settings.description: The deployment.environment.name every record carries (for example production). Empty: not sent.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Deployment environment

settings.description: How many records may wait for export per signal. When it is full, new records are dropped and counted; a request never waits for export.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export queue (records per signal)

settings.description: The most records sent in one request to the receiver.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export batch size

settings.description: How long one send to the receiver may take. A save waits for a send in flight, up to this, while the pipeline restarts.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Export timeout (seconds)

settings.description: How long a failed batch is retried before its records are counted failed.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Retry horizon (seconds)

settings.description: How long waiting records are sent for when the pipeline stops (a save here, or shutdown) before the rest are counted dropped.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Drain deadline (seconds)

settings.description: How often metrics are sent.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Metric interval (seconds)

settings.description: The share of new traces sent (1.0 = all). A request that arrives inside a sampled trace follows its parent's decision.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Trace sampling ratio

settings.description: The most distinct series one metric may have; beyond it, series fold into one overflow series.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Series per metric

settings.description: Allow /api/probes/score results to be exported when the request also asks for it (export_results). Off: they never leave.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Allow stateless result export

settings.description: Which recorded results become log records: live, batch, both (live,batch), or empty for neither.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Result log origins

settings.description: A failure or drop within this long shows the signal as degraded in health.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Degraded window (seconds)

settings.description: Records waiting this long with no successful send show the signal as unavailable.
settings.effect: next export; drains and restarts the export pipeline
settings.label: Unavailable after (seconds)

validators.description: Length and character set only (no check digit): the normalised value's length is one of lengths and every character is in the charset (digits: 0-9; upper_alnum: 0-9 and A-Z).
Luhn (ISO/IEC 7812-1 Annex B) check digit over ASCII digits; spaces and hyphens are ignored; at least two digits.

Reads whether a candidate is a MASKED value of a format (valid = masked): one mask character (X x * # • ● █) with kept digits only at the start and end, filling the format's length in a popular layout.

ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 over ASCII digits and upper-case letters (A=10 ... Z=35); valid when the number mod 97 is 1. The rearranging mode first moves the first four characters to the end (the ISO 13616 rearrangement); rearrange=none checks the value as written.
10 digits: a mod 11 check digit over weights 10 to 2
9 digits: area, group and serial range rules (no check digit)
Verhoeff check digit (dihedral group D5) over ASCII digits; spaces and hyphens are ignored; at least two digits.
Weighted sum check: exactly one digit per weight and sum(digit_i * weight_i) mod modulus is 0, the check digit last (check_position=last). Weights and modulus are the rule set's.
